claims.text: The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
A composite or gradient architecture can introduce a heterogeneous microstructure into HfZrTiTa0.53.
Introducing a heterogeneous microstructure will enhance strain hardening in HfZrTiTa0.53 under adiabatic dynamic deformation.
Introducing a heterogeneous microstructure will improve uniform deformability in HfZrTiTa0.53 under adiabatic dynamic deformation.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 15% relative to the stated baseline.
The intervention will increase uniform deformation by 20% relative to the baseline.
The intervened alloy will have a strain-rate sensitivity coefficient between 0.02 and 0.05.
The prediction applies over strain rates from 10^3 to 10^4 s^-1.
The predicted improvements depend on the specific microstructural modification and alloying addition.
A matched comparison should test HfZrTiTa0.53 with and without the heterogeneous microstructure under dynamic deformation.
The hypothesis is falsified if both yield strength and uniform deformation fail to increase by at least 10% relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 15% higher yield strength and 20% higher uniform deformation, but the falsification rule accepts increases of only 10% in each. Outcomes between 10% and the predicted values would miss the quantitative prediction without falsifying it.

The numerical baseline is explicitly quasi-static, whereas the prediction and experiment concern high-rate dynamic loading. Comparing the intervention directly with the quasi-static values would confound the intervention effect with strain-rate effects and is not a fully matched baseline-versus-intervention comparison.
